newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Southcorp reports strong wine sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Southcorp reports strong wine sales.

text.p: Australian wine and packaging group Southcorp Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday its wine division recorded strong growth in local and international sales in its first quarter ended September 30.

"The group recorded strong domestic and international sales growth in the first quarter and is confident about performance in the balance of the year (ending June 30, 1997)," Southcorp Wines chief executive Bruce Kemp said in a statement.

Kemp told Reuters later that a good vintage this year was overcoming supply constraints which emerged from last year's drought-affected season and said increased production volumes would drive further sales growth.

"The market is really responding to better availability, which is really an opportunity we are exploiting at the moment," he said after announcing a A$700,000 expansion of Southcorp's recently acquired Coldstream Hill winery in Victoria state.
The expansion would double capacity at the winery to 1,000 tonnes of grape in time for the 1997 vintage, he said.

Southcorp, which earned A$90 million before interest and tax in 1995/96 on sales revenue of A$447 million, was hoping for some fall in the price of grapes to prevent the company's products being priced out of key international markets, he said.
"Demand is expanding faster than we can," Kemp said.
"Certainly, we can't see supply and demand being met inside five years for super premium wines," he added.
Kemp declined to give figures on the first quarter performance and said these would be given at the group's annual meeting in Adelaide on November 22.
